1rsy07a:429: The layered memory system (short-term / mid-term / long-term) is the most engineering-intensive part of OpenClaw's multi-agent architecture. Short-term memory leverages the LLM's own context window; mid-term memory uses dated transaction journals (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md); long-term memory stores cross-session core information in MEMORY.md. The benefit of this layering is clear physical isolation of information with different lifecycles: high-frequency information that doesn't need persistence (current session context) lives in the context window; mid-frequency information (operation records from recent days) is handled by the file system; low-frequency but long-lived information (user preferences, core rules) goes into MEMORY.md. This design avoids the maintenance complexity of a single monolithic memory system and allows retrieval and update strategies for each level to be optimized independently. Notably, the author treats "remembering the workflow" as one of the core contents of long-term memory in practice — this effectively externalizes the agent's standard operating procedure (SOP) into an editable file, so behavior adjustments require neither retraining nor prompt modification, only updating the corresponding Markdown file.
